result.title: Output-Aware Block Influence: Jacobian-Lens Weighting for Depth Pruning
result.summary: Depth pruning removes entire transformer blocks and therefore depends on a reliable criterion for identifying which blocks can be removed. Block Influence (BI) ranks blocks by how minimally they rotate the hidden state. However, local redundancy does not necessarily imply downstream irrelevance. We address this limitation using the Jacobian Lens (J-Lens) neural artifact, a map transporting perturbations at a layer to the final residual stream. At a common sparsity level, pruning scores applying J-Lens transportation to $BI$, what we call $J-BI$, were found to improve post-pruning accuracy by up to 19 points over $BI$ while reducing damage to perplexity for Qwen3-8B, Llama-3.1-8B-IT, and Gemma-3-12B-IT. We also perform a single-block ablation study and use J-Lens probing to explain why the proposed scores improved performance.

AI.brief_summary: 针对 depth pruning 中 Block Influence 只衡量局部冗余、未必对应下游无关性的问题，作者用 Jacobian Lens 把各层扰动传输到最终残差流，据此对 BI 分数加权（J-BI），并在 Qwen3-8B、Llama-3.1-8B-IT、Gemma-3-12B-IT 上报告剪枝后精度提升，另用单块消融与 J-Lens 探测解释原因。
AI.relevance_reason: 其用 Jacobian 把中间层状态的影响线性映射到最终输出，可作为核查 latent 推理中中间状态或推理步「贡献分配」的度量线索；但论文面向纯文本压缩，与视觉证据、推理轨迹无直接关联，迁移性需要验证。
